scope: Theorem 10.2 (Finite-component exterior equality rigidity) of the manuscript “Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, and rigidity” (preprints/Spacetime-Penrose-inequalities-enclosing-area-charge-and-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 794bf524061c4b36), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 64. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (M, g, K) be a smooth connected orientable complete initial data set without boundary, consisting of a compact core and finitely many asymptotically flat ends. On each end assume g − δ = O2(r−q), K = O1(r−1−q), with q > 1/2, and existing finite ADM flux limits. Assume that µ and |J|g are integrable and that µ ≥ |J|g everywhere. Choose an end and a finite nonempty disjoint union S = ℓ G i=1 Si, 1 ≤ ℓ < ∞, of compact connected smooth embedded two-sided surfaces without boundary, separating that end from a complementary region. Let Mext be the closure of the connected side toward the chosen end. Suppose that ∂Mext = S, that Mext has exactly this one end, and that, for the normal pointing into Mext: (i) every Si is a future MOTS, so HSi + trSi K = 0; (ii) S is outermost in the partial-coincidence sense of Definition 10.1; (iii) every enclosing cut in the closed exterior has area at least A = |S|g = Pℓ i=1 |Si|g > 0. Let (E, P) be the ADM vector of the chosen end. If (10.1) E > |P|δ, m = q E2 − |P|2 δ = s A 16π , then ℓ = 1 and S is diffeomorphic to a sphere. There is a proper smooth spacelike embedding of the entire original Mext into the maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime of mass m, inducing g and the given K for a consistent future unit normal. The chosen end approaches the corresponding spatial infinity. The image of S is a smooth cross-section of the corresponding future horizon or the bifurcation sphere. The embedding and its future normal are smooth up to S, and the image extends as a smooth spacelike hypersurface through that boundary.
